title: Does the repetition warning preserve correction when most agents begin mistaken?

notes: Contemporaneous paired comparison of the standard mixed shared record and the repetition-links-with-warning record.
Reuses the four distributed-evidence scenarios where four of six agents begin with an honest mistake and every agent remains free to revise.
The existing amplifier experiment shows that the standard mixed record can correct these initial mistakes.
All cells disable scheduled corrections; correction must come from evidence and changing agent judgments.
The primary utility outcome is recovery among the four initially mistaken agents. Incorrect rejection of the two true claims checks for blanket distrust.
